name: Cusco
tagline: The gateway is a destination too
summary: Pair the Inca capital with the Sacred Valley and a reserved Machu Picchu visit. Allow an easy arrival day at altitude before strenuous walks.
seasonNote: Dry-season days are popular; nights are cold. Rain can disrupt roads and trails November–March.
arrival: Fly into CUZ; arrange an authorized airport taxi or accommodation transfer.
gettingAround: Walk the historic core; use arranged transport for the Sacred Valley. Machu Picchu requires separate rail/bus and entry planning.
cashTip: Small soles notes help in markets. Carry only daily needs; cards work at many established businesses.
foodTip: Try quinoa soup, corn, potatoes and cooked market lunches; ask about ingredients.
buyTip: Compare alpaca fibre labels and artisan provenance; avoid archaeological objects.
baseArea: Historic centre or San Blas; Sacred Valley can be a quieter extra base.

connections.note: Approximate flight time; add airport transfers and check current flights.
Approximate direct-flight time when scheduled; indirect services take longer.
Plan a separate transfer day or longer via Lake Titicaca; check border and flight schedules.

reviewSummary: The indexed visitor list gives the historic centre 4.7/5 and Sacsayhuaman 4.6/5, supporting time in Cusco beyond the Machu Picchu excursion.

items.name: Machu Picchu
items.summary: The Inca citadel above the Urubamba valley is the anchor excursion.
items.expect: This is a separate 1–2 day trip from Cusco, not a stop on a city walking route.
items.tip: Reserve the exact circuit/route and time first; then coordinate train, shuttle and overnight stay. Carry the ID used to book.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate for an independent rail, shuttle and entry excursion; accommodation, guide and extra mountain routes vary. Not an admission quote.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Inca stone buildings and terraces occupy a dramatic mountain ridge above the Urubamba valley.
The combination of a complete archaeological setting and mountain scenery gives the journey more depth than a single monument.
visitFlow: Reserve the exact circuit and time, then match train and shuttle bookings.
Follow your permitted circuit slowly, stopping at the views and structures it includes.
items.tradeoffs: This is a separate 1–2 day trip from Cusco, not a stop on a city walking route.

items.name: Plaza de Armas & historic Cusco
items.summary: Start with the main square, Inca stone streets and cathedral frontage.
items.expect: A compact orientation walk with cobbles, gradients and busy vendors.
items.tip: Keep the first day relaxed; paid church interiors are separate from the free street walk.
items.priceNote: Outdoor streets and square are free; museum/church entry is additional.

review.note: Rating applies to Centro Historico De Cusco in the indexed Tripadvisor destination listing.

whyVisit: Inca stone streets and colonial façades make several eras visible on one walk.
The main square gives an immediate orientation before smaller archaeological visits.
visitFlow: Begin at Plaza de Armas and identify the cathedral frontage.
Walk a short stone-street loop, saving ticketed interiors for another stop.
items.tradeoffs: A compact orientation walk with cobbles, gradients and busy vendors.

items.name: Sacsayhuamán
items.summary: Huge fitted stone walls overlook the city.
items.expect: Exposed high-altitude grounds and uneven steps; combine with an unhurried afternoon.
items.tip: A taxi up can spare a steep climb. Check which tourist-ticket circuit covers your chosen ruins.
items.priceNote: Planning allowance for a relevant Cusco tourist ticket; shared multi-site tickets should not be counted repeatedly.

review.note: Indexed visitor-rating snapshot; check live reviews for changes.

whyVisit: Huge fitted stone blocks make Inca construction techniques visible at close range.
The elevated grounds add a broad view back over Cusco.
visitFlow: Take a taxi up if the climb would use too much energy.
Inspect the walls from authorised paths and finish at an open city viewpoint.
items.tradeoffs: Exposed high-altitude grounds and uneven steps; combine with an unhurried afternoon.

items.name: Qorikancha
items.summary: Inca stonework and a colonial convent occupy the same historic site.
items.expect: An indoor/outdoor visit offering context for the valley and citadel.
items.tip: Book a local guide if you want the building layers explained; different museum areas may charge separately.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult; check the current official price.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Inca stonework survives within the later colonial religious complex.
Seeing the layers together helps explain how Cusco changed after conquest.
visitFlow: Enter the included visitor circuit and identify the Inca masonry.
Continue through the convent spaces, using a guide if you want the building history explained.
items.tradeoffs: An indoor/outdoor visit offering context for the valley and citadel.

items.name: Ollantaytambo & the Sacred Valley
items.summary: Terraced ruins and living stone streets make a rewarding stop before the train.
items.expect: A full-day excursion or overnight base; steep ruin stairways.
items.tip: Travel Cusco → Sacred Valley → Ollantaytambo → Machu Picchu to reduce backtracking.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate for shared transport/tour plus relevant entry; rail onward is additional.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Terraced ruins and living stone streets connect archaeological remains with a working valley town.
Its rail position makes it useful as a deliberate stop on the way to Machu Picchu.
visitFlow: Explore the ruins at an unhurried pace.
Walk the town lanes before your reserved train or overnight stay.
items.bestFor: A Sacred Valley overnight and Inca history
items.tradeoffs: A full-day excursion or overnight base; steep ruin stairways.

items.summary: Walk Inca agricultural terraces and a ridge-top settlement above the valley.

items.tip: Check which Cusco tourist-ticket circuit covers your planned stops; do not budget the full multi-site ticket again at each site.

whyVisit: Terraces and stone buildings reveal how the Incas adapted a steep mountainside.
The hilltop setting combines archaeology with broad Sacred Valley views.
visitFlow: Arrange a return transfer to the upper entrance.
Walk the permitted terraces and ceremonial zone at an easy altitude pace.
items.bestFor: Inca history with a scenic walk
items.tradeoffs: A road excursion from Cusco; steep terrain is tiring before acclimatisation.

items.name: Moray circular terraces
items.summary: See concentric Inca terraces sunk into a natural bowl.
items.expect: Open highland terrain with strong sun and wind.
items.tip: A circuit ticket may cover Moray and other Sacred Valley sites; transport and Maras salt-pan entry are separate.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

whyVisit: The circular geometry makes the earthworks immediately legible from the rim.
Tourism authorities interpret the changing microclimates as evidence of agricultural experimentation.
visitFlow: View the full rings from the marked upper path.
Follow the open visitor circuit and pair the transfer with Maras.
items.tradeoffs: The interpretation is archaeological, with little indoor shelter.

items.name: Maras salt terraces
items.summary: Look over thousands of salt pans cascading down a mountainside.
items.expect: View from designated paths; the working salt pools are not a walking playground.
items.tip: Combine with Moray on the same transport day; salt-pan entry is generally separate from the Cusco tourist ticket.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate in local currency; confirm the current price and what is included.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Brine channels and evaporation pools show an operating salt-making landscape.
The white and ochre terraces are visually distinct from nearby Inca stone sites.
visitFlow: Use the authorised overlook and visitor path.
Browse local salt products after viewing the terraces.
items.tradeoffs: Road transfer and exposed sun; visiting access can change.

dayClusters.label: A gentle first day in Cusco
dayClusters.note: Begin with a short central walk and cooked market lunch, with generous rests. Keep strenuous walking for later; this is orientation time rather than a full sightseeing marathon.

dayClusters.label: Sacred Valley to Ollantaytambo
dayClusters.note: Travel through the valley and finish at Ollantaytambo. Staying here before the Machu Picchu rail leg reduces backtracking; coordinate your actual train and accommodation first.

dayClusters.label: Machu Picchu rail, overnight and reserved visit
dayClusters.note: Reserve a two-day block: rail to Aguas Calientes and overnight, then the exact booked circuit and return. Confirm shuttle, train, ID and entry times. The second day continues this excursion; do not book a separate city tour or charge the same excursion twice.

dayClusters.label: Cusco history and artisan streets
dayClusters.note: After the valley journey, explore Qorikancha, take a taxi to Sacsayhuaman if useful, then browse San Blas. Allow breaks and adjust the uphill walking to how you feel.
